title: Does the news cover what actually kills us?
subtitle: Play newspaper editor and share out a hundred stories on causes of death, then watch the bars turn into what Americans actually died of.
form: allocate (split 100 stories over the bars, judge: false)
notes: b is the skeptic; a closes. Coverage and death shares from OWID's stacked chart (NYT 2023; 15 causes), rounded to whole numbers: coverage 3, 4, 42, 18, 33; deaths 29, 27, 1, 0 (16 deaths), 43. One bar_chart with two stages; the news values stay as dashed caps when the bars grow into deaths. The 18,000x is OWID's own published ratio (18,240x, shares within the 15 causes); the rounded stacked-chart shares (18 % of coverage, 16 of ~2.3 million deaths) don't reproduce it exactly, so it is said as 'about eighteen thousand times' and cited to OWID. Engine: the allocate's 'Stories left' readout replaces the task under the heading and the account bar label is tiny; terrorism's death bar reads 0 (no '<1' label option).
